text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Anti-Corruption Agency has arrested 16 people in Kuala Lumpur this year on various charges. Most of them were policemen and City Hall staff.

-- Economists are divided over the trend in the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange for the rest of the year. Some say good earnings growth, a stable ringgit and better-than-expected current account deficit would be positive surprises aiding a rally in the stock market. But, others said a negative sentiment would continue to prevail over the next few months due to a bleak economic outlook.
-- Bank Negara has indicated to local banks to consider shortening the period allowed for classifying loans as non-performing to three months from six after a default occurs.
-- Ringgit will not be allowed to depreciate very much to prevent an erosion in international competitiveness. This would help keep import costs down and force manufacturers to improve productivity.
